{{Quote|Rokko's about as civilized as a starving reek.|Laranth Tarak|<ref name="JT" />}}
'''Rokko''' was a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] who operated on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. A member of the [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii]] [[Kajidic/Legends|clan]], he operated mainly in the [[Yaam Sector]], trafficking in stolen merchandise. During this time, he had dealings with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] fugitive [[Jax Pavan]], initially hiring him to track down a [[Cerean/Legends|Cerean]] named [[Toh Revo Chryyx]] for him. However, in the process of attempting to apprehend the Cerean, Chryyx committed [[Death/Legends|suicide]], which led to Rokko refusing to pay Pavan. When Pavan used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to defend himself against Rokko's [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], the Hutt alerted sector police to the fugitive's presence, but Pavan was able to defeat the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] who were sent to arrest him.

Pavan later came to Rokko seeking help in locating the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[10-4TO]], which supposedly had information important to the group [[Whiplash]], a secret resistance organization opposed to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. Rokko agreed to help Pavan, believing that there would be a sizable reward for him. However, after a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] named [[Den Dhur]] arrived at Rokko's home with a droid named [[I-5YQ]], who knew Pavan, Rokko suspected Pavan's plea for help was a plot aimed at killing him. Though he had his bodyguards attack the group, he was forced to quickly order them to stand down after I-5 threatened to destroy his prize possessions, [[decelerated luminescent image]]s, rare pictures of Nal Hutta. Pavan and the others were then able to flee from the Hutt.

==Biography==
===First encounter with Pavan===
{{Quote|We are done here. The contract was unfulfilled, therefore payment is not forthcoming.|Rokko to Jax Pavan|<ref name="JT" />}}
Rokko was born approximately [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]]<ref name="DOB" /> on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]] into the [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii]] [[Kajidic/Legends|clan]]. At some point, Rokko moved to the capital [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where he established a small criminal empire, based in the [[Yaam Sector]] of [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]]. The [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] dealt mainly in stolen merchandise, and he built up a considerable fortune and made a name for himself on Coruscant.<ref name="JT" />

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Rokko hired the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] fugitive [[Jax Pavan]]&mdash;who was making a living as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]&mdash;to hunt down a [[Cerean/Legends|Cerean]] by the name of [[Toh Revo Chryyx]], promising to pay Pavan 15,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for Chryyx. However, the Cerean committed [[Death/Legends|suicide]] by stopping his heart after Pavan captured him. As the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] had specified that Chryyx be brought to him alive, Rokko reneged on his word. Pavan met with Rokko and two of his [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] in the [[Yaam Sector|Blackpit Slums]] section of the underlevels, where Pavan demanded he be paid, claiming it was not his fault the Cerean had killed himself. Rokko refused to pay the [[Human/Legends|Human]], insisting that the bounty had said Chryyx would be accepted alive only.<ref name="JT" />

When the Human again insisted that he was owed money, Rokko sent his two bodyguards&mdash;a [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] and a [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]]&mdash;to attack Pavan. However, Pavan used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to disarm the two, though that action revealed him as a Jedi. Now aware of this fact, Rokko contacted the local [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] sector police after the battle, hoping to collect the bounty on Pavan. Pavan defeated the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] sent to arrest him, and he suspected Rokko had sent them.<ref name="JT" />

===Request for help===
{{Quote|I need your aid in finding a lost droid.''"<br />"''And why should I do this?''"<br />"''Because there's a lot of credits in it for you.|Jax Pavan and Rokko|<ref name="JT" />}}
However, a few days later, Pavan showed up at Rokko's home, hoping to speak with the Hutt. Rokko allowed his [[Aegis-7 battle droid|Aegis-7]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] to admit Pavan and his comrade [[Laranth Tarak]], a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]]. Pavan promised to overlook the fact that Rokko had turned him in to the Empire if the Hutt would help them search for the droid [[10-4TO]]. The [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] was said to contain information valuable to [[Whiplash]], a group resisting the Empire in secret. Pavan tried to convince Rokko that the Empire would be willing to pay a large sum for it, although in reality the Jedi planned to give the droid to Whiplash.<ref name="JT" />

Although the Hutt considered turning Pavan in for the bounty on his head, he decided against it and agreed to consider helping the two. While he was mulling over the idea, a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] by the name of [[Den Dhur]] arrived at Rokko's home. Dhur claimed to have a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that was an expert at the card game [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]]. Intrigued, Rokko allowed Dhur and the droid, [[I-5YQ]], to enter. After playing the droid, the Hutt was stunned to find that it was able to beat him. He offered to pay Dhur 500 credits for it, realizing that it would be able to win many games against unsuspecting opponents, making money for the Hutt. After bargaining, the two settled on 1,000 credits.<ref name="JT" />

Before Dhur left, Rokko asked the droid to fetch Pavan and Laranth. Unknown to the Hutt was that Dhur was not planning on selling I-5; rather, it was a ruse so that the two could find information about Jax Pavan, the son of I-5's late [[Lorn Pavan|master]]. In his dying breath, Lorn Pavan had requested that I-5&mdash;whose intelligence bordered on [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]]&mdash;help take care of his son should a need arise. Dhur and I-5 hoped that Rokko would be able to aid them using his intelligence sources, and so used sabacc as a front. When I-5 encountered Pavan in Rokko's house, he immediately informed the Jedi that he had been looking for him, per a request from Pavan's father.<ref name="JT" />

Stunned to hear that a droid was going to tell him about his father and [[Darth Maul/Legends|how]] Lorn Pavan had died, Pavan marched away to Rokko's throne room. However, after the Hutt realized that the droid knew Pavan, he assumed that it was not mere coincidence&mdash;rather, he thought, it was a plot to kill him. He had his bodyguards move to attack them but was quickly forced to call them off. I-5 had activated his finger-laser and threatened to destroy Rokko's most prized possession&mdash;his collection of [[decelerated luminescent image]]s, works of the Hutt artist [[Gorgo]]. These were images frozen in time, as they were made of [[Prothium|protium]] gas exposed to Nal Hutta centuries ago. These were so thick it took light years to shine through, making them essentially "windows to the past". As Gorgo had died centuries ago, the images were extremely rare; in fact, Rokko owned the only such images in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="JT" />

Due to his prized possessions being threatened, the Hutt immediately called off his bodyguards and allowed the group to leave. However, as soon as they had reached the [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]], Rokko sent his Aegis-7 battle droid after them. The group was able to bring the ceiling down on the droid and escaped.<ref name="JT" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I should have known better than to trust a human.|Rokko|<ref name="JT" />}}
Rokko the Hutt was a greedy, merciless being, with little care for others. Jax Pavan once expressed the opinion that Rokko would sell out his mother for money, no matter the amount. Rokko attempted to turn Pavan over to the Empire simply because there was a bounty, though worth little, on his head. After Pavan came to him later, having survived the Empire's attempt to arrest him, Rokko agreed to work with him, as the Human had a business deal in mind. Though Rokko considered selling out Pavan once more, he decided that the effort was not worth it. Rokko was also described by Jax Pavan as cruel and merciless.<ref name="JT" />

However, Rokko did have a softer side. He loved art, particularly the works of the Hutt artist Gorgo, and would go to great lengths, even allowing his enemies to escape, in order to protect them. Rokko greatly admired Gorgo and showed genuine sadness that his works were almost extinct.<ref name="JT" />

==Behind the scenes==
Rokko was created by author [[Michael Reaves]] and appeared in the [[2008]] novel ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]'', the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars: Coruscant Nights]]'' trilogy.
